title: SLO Negotiation Field Lab & Decisions Journal
content:
SUMMARY:
This doc is a working "field lab" for negotiating SLOs across product, infra, serving-runtime, and customer success. It's intentionally pragmatic: run experiments to produce concrete data for trade-offs, keep a running decision journal, and produce 2 recommended SLO bundles (conservative & performance) for pilot services.

OBJECTIVES (why this exists):
- Surface the real service-level trade-offs that product teams accept when faced with latency/cost constraints.
- Provide an evidence-first negotiation playbook so SREs + product can move beyond opinion.
- Run 6 experiments in the next 12 weeks to gather p50/p95/p99, error-type breakdown, and cost per 1k requests for each SLO candidate.
- Produce a short decision journal with stakeholder sign-offs and rollback criteria.

BACKGROUND / CONTEXT NOTES (notes to self):
- We keep seeing feature teams set unrealistic p99 targets to match marketing claims; ops then overprovisions.
- Need a small set of measurable SLO bundles (latency-focused, cost-focused, mixed) to standardize negotiation.
- This is a cross-functional pilot with two product teams (chat API, embeddings service) as guinea pigs.

SCOPE:
- In-scope: SLO discovery & negotiation for two pilot services; automated experiment harness; decision journal entries; rollout checklist templates.
- Out-of-scope: company-wide policy, billing changes, SLA legal text (we'll produce recommendations only).

SUCCESS METRICS (how we measure success):
- Experiment completion: 6 experiments executed and analyzed within 12 weeks.
- Decision clarity: for each pilot service a single chosen SLO bundle with written justification and acceptance criteria.
- Cost delta transparency: % change in token cost per 1k requests for changes to model/quantization/batching.
- Oncall churn: a reduction in emergent paging incidents tied to SLO misalignment for the pilot services over 90 days.

STAKEHOLDERS & ROLES (working roles, not org chart):
- SRE Lead (owner): Aisha Kapoor — run experiments, shepherd data collection, maintain decision journal.
- Product Lead (negotiation partner): Miguel Ortega — defines user-facing constraints, signs off on risk.
- Serving Runtime Eng: Samira Chen — provides kernel/quantization recommendations and experimental knobs.
- Cost Analyst / Finance contact: Evan Brooks — verifies cost math and reporting.
- Solutions / CS: Priya Nair — represents customer expectations and enterprise risk.

COMMUNICATIONS & CADENCE:
- Weekly Lab Standup (30m): Mon 10:00am. Quick status, blockers, next 7 days. Owner rotates.
- Bi-weekly Stakeholder Demo (45m): Show experiment results, decision log updates.
- Slack channel: #sre-field-lab-slo (use for fast Qs and artifacts).

12-WEEK FIELD LAB TIMELINE (high level):
- Week 0 (prep, 1 week): finalize pilots, create experiment harness, agree on signals. Tickets: AIINF-1423 (prep infra), AIINF-1424 (pilot config).
- Weeks 1–4 (exploration): run baseline load tests (p50/p95/p99, tails, evictions). Capture CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates.
- Weeks 5–8 (interventions): run targeted experiments — batching changes, quantization toggles, prefix caching, model fallback.
- Weeks 9–10 (negotiation rounds): present data-driven trade-offs to product, iterate on SLO bundle selection.
- Weeks 11–12 (closure): finalize decision journal entries, produce rollout checklist, and schedule pilot rollout.

EXPERIMENT TEMPLATE (short form to copy/paste):
- Experiment title: <short phrase>
- Hypothesis: "If we X then Y (metric) will change by Z%"
- Service: <chat-api | embeddings>
- Knob(s): [list — e.g., batching=200ms cap, quantize=int8, KV_cache=true]
- Measurement window: 72 hours steady-state with synthetic + production-shadow traffic
- Signals to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, infra cost estimator (GPU-hours + memory delta), token emissions per request, cache hit rate, error taxonomy
- Acceptance criteria: e.g., p95 <= 220ms AND cost delta <= +8%
- Notes: (freeform)

NEGOTIATION SCRIPT (for SRE <> Product meeting):
- Opening: "Our goal is to pick a measurable SLO we can enforce with clear rollback rules. We're not asking you to accept a number in the meeting — we're here to align trade-offs."
- Present baseline: show p95/p99 and current cost per 1k (visual).
- Trade-off slide: rows: SLO bundle (conservative / balanced / performance), columns: p50/p95/p99, infra cost delta, expected user impact, rollback triggers.
- Ask product: "Which user experience (latency percentile) drives retention?"
- Probe: "What's the minimum SLA we must promise for paid customers vs free tier?"
- Close: agree on 1 or 2 candidate bundles to validate in Week 9 negotiation round.

DECISION JOURNAL (living log — examples):
- 2026-05-14 — Entry by Aisha: Baseline collected for chat-api. p95=340ms, p99=1.2s during peak. KV cache not yet enabled. Initial hypothesis: batching and KV cache will reduce p95 by ~30% without significant cost increase. Miguel + Samira online.
- 2026-05-21 — Entry by Samira: Batch cap 200ms lowered p95 to 230ms in synthetic test and reduced GPU throughput by 18%. Observed slight increase in p50 (small tailing effects).
- 2026-05-28 — Entry by Evan: Cost model shows GPU-hour delta would be +5% for the performance bundle, but token cost per 1k requests unchanged if cache hit > 40%.
- 2026-06-02 — Entry by Miguel: Product prefers balanced bundle for free tier and performance bundle as opt-in for enterprise customers. Requests written acceptance for negotiation round on 2026-06-09.

ESCALATION & ROLLBACK SCRIPT (short):
- Condition: sustained p95 > negotiated SLO for 30m AND error rate > 2x baseline.
- Immediate: flip traffic to fallback model variant (pre-registered): serving-runtime toggle: fallback-variant-A.
- Pager: notify oncall SRE and product lead + CS for impacted customers.
- Postmortem: capture decision in journal within 48 hours, include timeline and mitigation steps.

CHECKLISTS (quick):
- Pre-experiment checklist: infra tickets created, monitoring dashboards exist, golden user scenario identified, data retention window set.
- Pre-rollout checklist: decision journal entry approved, runbook created, canary size defined, rollback plan validated, oncall notified.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS (notes):
- How to represent user-perceived latency vs server p95? Need UX input — Priya to advise.
- Enterprise customers frequently require a written SLA clause; this pilot will need legal review before any SLA commitment.
- Observability gaps: we lack per-request token-cost tagging in prod traces; temporary sampling may be required.

TODOs (short list):
- [Aisha] Finish experiment harness PR and attach to AIINF-1423 — due 2026-05-17.
- [Samira] Produce recommended quantization profiles for chat-api and embeddings — due 2026-05-20.
- [Evan] Finalize cost per 1k calculator and tutorial — due 2026-05-24.
- [Miguel] Draft product-tier acceptance criteria (free vs paid) — due 2026-05-26.

ARTIFACTS TO PRODUCE BY CLOSE (deliverables):
- Decision journal PDF with signed acceptance for pilot services.
- Experiment appendix CSVs + graphs (p50/95/99, cost curves).
- Rollout checklist + runbook for each pilot.
- Short 1-page recommendation memo for executive summary.

NOTES / VOICE:
- Keep this doc deliberately lightweight and timestamp every decision entry.
- Encourage short, evidence-backed opinions; avoid long hypothesis chains without data.
- Use the field lab to codify negotiation language that can be templated for other teams.

APPENDIX: example trade-off table (format to paste in slides)
- Bundle name | p50 | p95 | p99 | infra delta | user-impact notes | rollback trigger
- Conservative | 120ms | 300ms | 650ms | -6% | minimal user impact | p95 > 350ms for 30m
- Balanced | 100ms | 220ms | 480ms | +2% | smoother tails | p95 > 260ms for 20m
- Performance | 70ms | 160ms | 320ms | +8% | best UX for paid users | p95 > 180ms for 10m

END NOTES:
- Next stakeholder demo scheduled 2026-06-09.
- Keep decision journal entries short and link to raw CSVs in linked_artifacts.

---
This is a working doc; expect typos. If you're reading this and want to contribute, add a new decision entry and include a short summary of experiments run and the ticket that executed them.
